title: Why AI Data Centers Are Replacing Air With Liquid

lines.text: Modern AI is limited by heat, not just computing power.
lines.label: THE REAL LIMIT

lines.text: NVIDIA's GB200 rack needs about one hundred twenty kilowatts.
lines.label: 120 KW / RACK

lines.text: About eighty five percent of its cooling is liquid.
lines.label: 85% LIQUID

lines.text: The remaining cooling still uses air.
lines.label: 15% AIR

lines.text: Conventional room air cannot carry away enough heat alone.
lines.label: AIR ALONE

lines.text: This reveals the rule behind dense AI systems.
lines.label: DENSITY

lines.text: More chips create more heat in less space.
lines.label: MORE CHIPS

lines.text: Direct liquid cooling captures heat at the chip.
lines.label: DIRECT TO CHIP

lines.text: Sealed loops can recirculate coolant without evaporating water.
lines.label: CLOSED LOOP

lines.text: Water free often means no evaporative water use.
lines.label: NO EVAPORATION

lines.text: Dry coolers can reject heat with little water.
lines.label: DRY COOLERS

lines.text: Ignore heat, and chips can throttle to protect themselves.
lines.label: THROTTLING

lines.text: Air cooling then demands more fans and power.
lines.label: MORE POWER

lines.text: That turns a computing challenge into a building challenge.
lines.label: CHIP TO BUILDING

lines.text: Like a laptop, a hot chip slows down.
lines.label: SAME RULE

lines.text: AI progress is now a cooling design problem.
lines.label: THE NEW BOTTLENECK

lines.text: When you hear AI claims, ask how it is cooled.
lines.label: ASK THIS

lines.text: Look for direct liquid cooling and closed loops.
lines.label: WHAT TO LOOK FOR

lines.text: Modern AI is limited by heat, not just computing power.
